atoms.b: Britain’s recorded history begins with Julius Caesar’s invasion of Britain in ((++55_BC 64_AD 1066)), when Roman forces first arrived, though lasting control came later under the Roman Empire.

After Roman withdrawal in the 5th century, Anglo-((++Saxon Norman Roman)) kingdoms emerged, followed by Viking invasions and eventual unification under English kings. The Norman Conquest in 1066, in which William the Conqueror became ((++king queen viscount)), reshaped England’s ruling class and governance.

In 1215, the Magna Carta marked the first limitation of royal power by the nobility. In 1265, Simon de Montfort led the first English Parliament, expanding ((++political royal ordinary)) representation.
The late ((++medieval Roman Victorian)) period was dominated by conflict, culminating in the Wars of the Roses between rival royal houses, ending in 1485 with the rise of the Tudor dynasty.

text:
The Wars of the Roses (1455–1487) were a series of civil wars in England between the House of Lancaster (emblem: red rose) and the House of York (emblem: white rose), both from the Plantagenet dynasty.
They fought over the throne due to weak rule by Henry VI. The conflict ended when Henry VII defeated Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field and united both houses, forming the Tudor dynasty (emblem: red and white rose).

atoms.b: From the Tudor period to 1901, Britain experienced key religious and political changes. In 1534, the Act of Supremacy under Henry VIII marked the break with Catholicism and the Vatican and made the monarch head of the ((++Church Crown UK)). This was later stabilized by the Elizabethan Settlement under Elizabeth I, which secured the Anglican Church. The Elizabethan period was also marked by growing patriotism, expanding ((++trade illness weather)), and flourishing poetry and drama.

In 1688/89, the Glorious Revolution overthrew James II and established a constitutional monarchy. This shift was confirmed by the Bill of Rights, which gave Parliament central political ((++power opinions will)). In the 1700s, the Enlightenment brought ((++new bad boring)) ideas in politics, philosophy, and science. In 1801, Ireland joined the United Kingdom. By 1901, Britain had developed into a stable parliamentary state.

Enlightenment – Aufklärung
Eine um 1700 einsetzende Epoche in der Geschichte Europas und Nordamerikas. Die aufklärerische Bewegung beabsichtigte eine grundlegende Veränderung des Denkens, bei der die menschliche Vernunft (Rationalität) zum Maßstab allen Handelns erklärt wurde.

atoms.title: Rise to World Power: Naval Power & Colonial Expansion

atoms.text: Great Britain’s rise to global power was driven by naval strength, political stability, and colonial expansion. In 1588, the defeat of the Spanish Armada marked the beginning of its emergence as a major naval power. The founding of the British East India Company in 1600 supported overseas trade and empire-building.

atoms.text: Political changes such as the Bill of Rights in 1689 strengthened Parliament, while the Act of Union in 1707 created Great Britain as a unified state including the kingdom of England and Scotland. Between about 1760 and 1830, the Industrial Revolution gave Britain economic and technological advantages.

atoms.text: In 1763, the Treaty of Paris made it the leading colonial power, despite losing the American colonies in 1776 during the American Revolution. Finally, victory over Napoleon Bonaparte at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815 marked the start of the Pax Britannica, the height of the British Empire's hegemony.
